name: Popconfirm
description: A lightweight anchored confirmation for small destructive or irreversible actions.
usage:
<Popconfirm
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Remove member</Button>}
  title="Remove Avery?"
  message="They lose access to this workspace."
  tone="danger"
  confirmText="Remove"
  onConfirm={() => undefined}
/>

anatomy.description: The control whose action needs a quick confirmation, like "Remove member".
The popover-anchored surface that stays near the trigger without blocking the page.
A short question naming the target plus one line of consequence.
The inline choice pair; tone="danger" marks irreversible confirms.

dos: Use for small row-level actions like removing a member or discarding a draft.
Phrase the title as a question that names the target, like "Remove Avery?".
Keep the message to one line of consequence.
donts: Don't use a popconfirm for severe or hard-to-reverse consequences; use AlertDialog.
Don't stack popconfirms or open one from inside a popover.
Don't use it for informational content; there is nothing to confirm.

examples.title: Inline confirmation
examples.description: Built on Popover, so it anchors to the trigger without taking over the page.

examples.title: Neutral action
examples.description: Without tone, the confirm suits routine decisions like publishing a report.

guidance.useWhen: A small action benefits from confirmation without a modal.
guidance.avoidWhen: The consequence is severe; use AlertDialog.
guidance.behavior: Anchored to its trigger and dismisses on confirm, cancel, or Escape.
guidance.responsive: The panel stays within the viewport near the trigger.

keyboard.action: Closes the popconfirm and returns focus to the trigger.
Moves focus to the confirm and cancel actions inside the panel.

notes: Built on Popover, so the panel is anchored to the trigger and the page stays interactive.
The trigger exposes aria-expanded for the confirmation panel.
Confirm and cancel are real buttons; the choice is never implicit.
